figures.caption: Hopper feeds the elevator, which lifts bottles into the main body (upper disk + selectors) and out via the exit conveyor (§2, p.15–27).
HMI screen (Information/Alarms/Production/Adjustments), Start/Stop/Reverse/Reset, Emergency stop, the two selectors and the pilot lights (§3.1–3.2, p.30–35).
The rotating upper disk carries the selectors/segments that pick each bottle and drop it, oriented, through its funnel (§2.2, p.16–21).
Bottles descend through the funnels helped by a constant air jet fed through a factory-set regulator; changing it can cause malfunctions (§4.1.2, p.62).
Before maintenance: lock the main switch OFF and the air valve closed, each with your padlock, and hang the danger tag (§8.8, p.136).
The front door reaches the segments/funnels for format changes; the side door is for inspection; both interlock while running (§2.2 / §3.3, p.20).
A detection system (camera or rack) reads each bottle; a servo-driven U-fork with guides turns it so all bottles exit the same way, inside an interlocked cabin (§2.4, p.26–27).
